## Observations

1. With \(P_0=0\) and \(P_r=\sum_{i=1}^r A_i\), each nonempty range sum is \(P_r-P_j\) for exactly one pair \(0\le j<r\le N\).
2. For a fixed right endpoint \(r\), the binomial theorem gives \((P_r-P_j)^K=\sum_{t=0}^K(-1)^t\binom Kt P_r^{K-t}P_j^t\). Summing over \(j<r\) therefore requires only the \(K+1\) sums of earlier prefix powers.
3. The zeroth power contributes \(1\) for every prefix, including a zero prefix. Inserting the current prefix after counting its contribution keeps the earlier-prefix sums restricted to \(j<r\).
4. Addition, subtraction, and multiplication preserve congruence modulo \(998244353\), and the powers of a prefix through degree \(K\) can be generated by successive multiplication.

## Solution sketch

1. “With \(P_0=0\) and \(P_r=\sum_{i=1}^r A_i\), each nonempty range sum is \(P_r-P_j\) for exactly one pair \(0\le j<r\le N\).” Read \(N\) and \(K\), then process the elements in order. Start the running prefix and the answer at zero. At each element, add it to the running prefix to obtain the prefix for that right endpoint.

2. “The zeroth power contributes \(1\) for every prefix, including a zero prefix. Inserting the current prefix after counting its contribution keeps the earlier-prefix sums restricted to \(j<r\).” Maintain \(S_t=\sum_{j<r}P_j^t\) for \(0\le t\le K\). Before the first element, the only earlier prefix is \(P_0\), so initialize \(S_0=1\) and every other entry to zero. This includes ranges starting at the first element and also handles \(N=1\).

3. “For a fixed right endpoint \(r\), the binomial theorem gives \((P_r-P_j)^K=\sum_{t=0}^K(-1)^t\binom Kt P_r^{K-t}P_j^t\). Summing over \(j<r\) therefore requires only the \(K+1\) sums of earlier prefix powers.” Precompute the signed coefficients \(c_t=(-1)^t\binom Kt\) once. For each new prefix, generate its powers \(Q_0=1\) and \(Q_e=Q_{e-1}P_r\) for \(1\le e\le K\). Add \(\sum_{t=0}^K c_t Q_{K-t}S_t\) to the answer, then add \(Q_t\) to each \(S_t\) for the next endpoint. If all elements are zero, each product in the contribution has a zero factor because \(K\ge 1\), so the answer is zero.

4. “Addition, subtraction, and multiplication preserve congruence modulo \(998244353\), and the powers of a prefix through degree \(K\) can be generated by successive multiplication.” Keep the running prefix, coefficients, powers, power sums, and answer reduced modulo \(998244353\). Print the answer after processing all \(N\) elements. The coefficients can be generated in \(O(K)\) time using the exact recurrence \(\binom K{t+1}=\binom Kt(K-t)/(t+1)\) before reduction. Each endpoint takes \(O(K)\) time, for \(O(NK)\) total time and \(O(K)\) auxiliary space beyond input storage.
